title.rendered: Fast by default: static pages that refresh themselves

excerpt.rendered: Static generation with time-based revalidation keeps pages instant while new posts still show up within minutes.

structured_blocks.name: core/paragraph
structured_blocks.html: Every page is generated ahead of time, so visitors get plain HTML from the edge. Next.js re-fetches WordPress in the background on a schedule and swaps the page when something changed.

title.rendered: Blocks as data, not just HTML

excerpt.rendered: The plugin exposes every block with its name and attributes, so the front end can render custom blocks as real components.

structured_blocks.name: core/paragraph
structured_blocks.html: By default the REST API returns content.rendered: one long HTML string. That works for paragraphs and images, but a custom block deserves more than a string.

excerpt.rendered: Editors keep the WordPress they know, developers get a modern React front end. Here is when that trade-off pays off.

structured_blocks.name: core/paragraph
structured_blocks.html: Headless WordPress splits the job in two: WordPress stays the place where content is written and organised, and a separate front end, here Next.js, decides how it looks and how fast it loads.

structured_blocks.html: Sites that need top performance, a design system shared with an app, or several front ends fed from one editorial team. For a simple brochure site, a classic theme is still the faster route.
